findings.text: The action-handler branch now emits `command:<name>` on `this.parent` instead of `this`. A top-level program with an action handler has no parent, so it no longer emits the event, and listeners registered with `program.on('command:'+name)` stop firing. Subcommands also now emit on the parent, so a listener on the subcommand itself no longer fires.

The new `else if (this.parent && this.parent.listenerCount(commandEvent))` branch runs before the operands, `*` and help/unknown handling. A subcommand with no action handler whose parent has any `command:<name>` listener now only emits to the parent. For example, `prog sub extra` skips the `*` dispatch and the missing-handler help or unknown-command handling for `sub`.

0.reason: This is deliberate legacy behaviour: the patch marks it `// legacy`, and from my knowledge of upstream Commander (the context files were missing, so I could not check the old code), `command:<name>` listeners are registered on the parent, so emitting there restores that contract and does not break a real use.

1.reason: The patch deliberately treats a parent `command:<name>` listener as the action handler for a subcommand that has none (marked `// legacy`), so skipping the `*`, help and unknown-command handling in that case is intended.
